text:
What have I left to give, my life already given?

If seed, scattered into another furrow,

if sap, spilled over every soil,

if flame, burned in every vessel of darkness.


What have I left to give, my death

as well? In every dream, in every day;

my vertical death, my deaf death

that no one knows yet belongs to me.


What have I left to give, if in giving I give

-and because it is mine, and from now on

if God does not hold me back or cut off

my clumsy hands- my resurrection...!

translation.title: What Have I Left to Give, My Life Already Given?...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's escalating gift-language, ending in resurrection as the last thing left to give.
